detailed_description: The Color Extractor analyzes one selected image in the browser and builds a simple color palette from canvas pixel data. After choosing an image file, you can set the number of colors from 5 to 10, click Extract Colors, review the image preview, and see the most frequent quantized colors with hex, RGB, and approximate percentage values. Each palette row can be clicked to copy the hex value, and the generated palette can be downloaded as a PNG swatch image. The tool works locally with FileReader and canvas, but it does not use machine learning, K-means clustering, color-space selection, drag-and-drop upload, multiple output formats, or precise professional color matching.
usage_steps: Choose one image file from your device.
Adjust the color count slider from 5 to 10 if needed.
Click Extract Colors to process a scaled canvas version of the image.
Review the palette rows with hex, RGB, and approximate percentage values.
Click a color row to copy its hex value, or download the palette as a PNG swatch.
usage_examples: Extract a quick hex palette from a logo or screenshot for a prototype.
Compare the most common quantized colors in a selected reference image.
Copy a hex value from an uploaded image for a small design draft.
Download a PNG swatch image after reviewing the generated browser-side palette.
